tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

beggs-graph-hermitian-start: Abstract, p.1: the paper states its own approach (start from a hermitian metric compatible connection).
beggs-graph-generalised-metrics: Section 2.1, p.5: the paper states it works with nondegenerate generalised metrics and does not impose the symmetries.
beggs-graph-geodesic-eqs-classical: Section 1, eqs (1)-(2), p.2: the paper sets out the geodesic velocity and amplitude flow equations it works with (framework from its cited earlier works).
beggs-graph-driving-force-novelty: Section 1, pp.2-3: the paper states what it adds, the imaginary driving force F, with F=0 recovering the earlier condition.
beggs-graph-reality-not-automatic: Section 2.2, p.6: the paper states how it handles reality of X (improved auxiliary equation or imaginary F). Prop 4.1 later shows the two equations differ.
beggs-graph-calculus-def: Section 3, p.7: the paper defines the graph calculus, bimodule structure and d.
beggs-graph-metric-def: Section 3, eq (10), pp.7-8: the paper defines the graph metric by coefficients lambda on arrows.
beggs-graph-prop31-hermitian-connections: Proposition 3.1, p.8: stated with the nondegeneracy condition and proved on the same page (K = GL, L Hermitian).
beggs-graph-prop32-torsion: Proposition 3.2, p.9: stated with its conditions; the proof follows on the page and covers the square condition and the minimal-calculus torsion.
beggs-graph-star-length-ratio: Proof of Theorem 3.4, p.11: the i=j case is derived in full and gives the ratio lambda_{0->i}/lambda_{i->0} = 1/sqrt(n) as a necessary condition. The Dynkin comparison is the authors' remark.
beggs-graph-star-relax-calculus: Section 3.1, p.12: the paper states that its non-existence result is specific to the minimal calculus and that more solutions could exist with a smaller quotient.
beggs-graph-star-n2-mobius: Theorem 3.4(b), p.11 and the n=2 end of its proof, p.12: eq (21) for n=2 is solved for the ratio, giving the Mobius relation between s1 and s2.
beggs-graph-prop41-velocity-eq: Proposition 4.1, p.13: the proof substitutes (26) and (23) into (8) and conjugates for real X; the difference is the improved auxiliary equation.
beggs-graph-force-minimal-assumption: Section 4, p.14: the paper states its own assumption on F.
beggs-graph-prop42-divergence: Proposition 4.2, p.14: stated and proved on pp.14-15 (div of the dual basis, the divergence condition, the canonical star). The value gives it in words, the formulas are not in the value.
beggs-graph-prop51-4star-eq: Proposition 5.1, p.16: the proof substitutes the found F (28) into the velocity equation of Prop 4.1 for the n=4 QLC of Theorem 3.4. A derivation by substitution, shown.
beggs-graph-4star-divcompat-limit: Remark 5.3, p.17: the paper states that divergence compatibility on the 4-star forces the lambda to sum to zero, so no Euclidean signature and a non-positive measure, a problem for the probabilistic reading.
beggs-graph-cayley-inner: Proposition 6.2, p.19: stated (alpha = 0, so inner) and proved on pp.19-20 without the left-invariance assumption of [4].
beggs-graph-cayley-lemma61: Lemma 6.1, p.19: stated with its iff condition and proved on the page, using the cited formula dh = -Gamma h - h Gamma* and antihermitian theta.
beggs-graph-cayley-prop62-bimodule: Proposition 6.2, p.19: stated with its condition (C closed under inversion, Cayley graph setup) and proved on pp.19-20.
beggs-graph-cayley-lemma63-star: Lemma 6.3, p.20: stated and proved from the formula of Proposition 6.2; alpha = 0 gives star-preserving.
beggs-graph-cayley-prop64-divergence: Proposition 6.4, p.22: stated for metric-compatible connections and proved on pp.22-23. The value gives it in words, the formulas are not in the value.
beggs-graph-cayley-prop65-velocity: Proposition 6.5, p.23: stated with its conditions and proved on the same page by direct computation.
beggs-graph-z-n4-open: Section 7, p.25: the paper states that uniqueness of the QLC for n=4 with the bigger calculus is not known.
beggs-graph-no-dirac-operators: Section 1, p.1: the paper states it does not consider Dirac operators or Connes' approach.
review-scope-four-domains: Abstract and Section I, p.1: the review states the four domains it covers.
three-families-defined: Abstract, p.1: the paper states the three families it studies.
zeno-effect-definition: Section 1, p.2: the paper defines Zeno effect and Zeno dynamics.
scope-unstructured-search-only: Section 1, p.2: the paper states it studies unstructured search only.
structure-caveat-unstructured-search: Section 1, p.3: the paper states the caveat that real problems have structure and unstructured search only indicates a possible advantage.
single-avoided-crossing-model-setup: Section 2.1, pp.4-5: the paper states the model it builds on and its schedule f = cot(pi tau). The coverage claim is attributed to earlier work and rests on it.
invariant-strategy-three-steps: Section 2.2, p.6: the paper states the three-step protocol it applies in every later section.
dissipation-into-ground-state-excluded: Section 2.2, p.7: the paper states it does not address dissipation into the ground state.
purity-argument-does-not-cover-zeno-regi: Section 4.1, p.11: the paper states its own purity argument does not strictly apply to the Zeno regime.
projective-measurements-no-continuum-lim: Section 4.1, p.11: the paper states the finite-measurement algorithm has no well-defined continuum limit.
decoherence-by-random-time-reversal-mode: Section 4.2, p.12: the paper defines the coin-flip decoherence model it uses.
master-equation-derivation-approximation: Appendix E.1, pp.28-29: the paper states the approximations (q >> 1, small change in f, many prior reversals) its derivation assumes.
destructive-measurement-no-purity-argume: Section 5.1, p.15: the paper states the purity argument is not available for destructive measurements.
dissipation-model-von-neumann-qubit-abor: Section 5.2, p.16: the paper defines the dissipation model (extra qubit, abort on |1>).
berwald-2024-numerical-methods-setup: Section 6, p.18: the paper states its software and the 21x21 symmetric-subspace size.
limitations-finite-size-and-interactions: Section 7, p.19: the paper states what it did not study and that the models are harder to implement.
encoding-and-hardware-out-of-scope: Sections 7-8, pp.20-21: the paper states encoding and hardware are out of scope.
single-avoided-crossing-limits-constant-: Appendix C, p.24: the paper states a drawback of its model (no constant-factor information).
zeno-three-level-unit-setup: Section 2, p.6: the paper defines its three-level unit and protocol.
zeno-forbidden-state-sweep: Section 2, p.6, eqs 2-3: the paper defines the swept coupling state and the allowed subspace under strong coupling.
zeno-ising-perfect-projection-assumption: Section 3, p.10: the paper states the assumption its Ising result depends on.
zeno-frustration-definition: Section 1, p.3: the paper defines a frustrated system.
zeno-dissipation-as-antihermitian: Section 4.1, p.11, eqs 14-16: the paper defines its decay model as an effective anti-Hermitian generator; the norm statement follows from the definition with positive rates.
zeno-dissipative-single-destroyed-state-: Section 4.1, p.11: the paper states the simplification it makes.
zeno-sat-numerical-instance: Section 4.1, p.12 and Appendix B: the paper states the instance it simulates and how it built it.
zeno-iterative-solver-feasibility-limit: Appendix D, p.33: the paper states its iterative solver is unlikely to be technically feasible.
zeno-three-hot-numerical-setup: Section 5, p.18, eq 22: the paper states the field vector and the two solution states.
zeno-errors-discussion: Section 6.1, pp.21-22: the paper states the error concern for three- and four-level units and the need to justify complexity.
zeno-numerical-methods: Section 7, p.22: the paper states its software, steps, projection threshold and compute time.
zeno-sat-clause-forbids-state: Appendix C, p.30: the paper defines how a clause forbids states and when a clause counts as satisfied.
zeno-one-hot-scalability-limit: Appendix E.1, p.34: the paper states a single one-hot system is classically samplable, so scalable use needs several subsystems.
biobank-datasets-described: Slide 'Medical databases and biobanks', p.10: the deck states the datasets and sizes it describes and later analyses. The figures are the deck's own statements.

theory_low.beggs-graph-prop33-star-compat: Proposition 3.3, p.10: the proof only treats the star-preserving part and cites [4, Prop 8.11]; the reduction of star-compatibility to the sum condition is not derived.
theory_low.beggs-graph-alpha-zero-qlc: Section 3, p.10: a remark resting on cited general results for inner calculi ([4, Prop 8.11]), not proved in this paper.
theory_low.beggs-graph-star-theorem34: Theorem 3.4, pp.10-12: the ratio condition and alpha = 0 are derived, but the bound n at most 4 rests on the remaining relations being 'checked' to hold for n=3,4 and fail for n>=5, with no working shown.
theory_low.beggs-graph-star-counts-n2-3-4: Section 1, p.2 and Theorem 3.4: the counts for n=3 and n=4 depend on the unshown check of the remaining relations; only the n=2 case is derived in the proof.
theory_low.beggs-graph-star-fail-n5: Proof of Theorem 3.4, p.12: the failure for n at least 5 is stated as 'can be checked' with no working in the paper.
theory_low.beggs-graph-star-n2-dynkin: Remark 3.5, p.12: a comparison with earlier work [2] stated without the working; the match is the authors' claim.
theory_low.beggs-graph-4star-real-closure: Example 5.2, p.16: a remark inside one worked example (constant lambda, constant mu), no general proof.
